answer.stillOpen: This is institutional identity, terminology and routing, not 51 complete disciplinary procedures. Wyoming's Joint Rule 22-1 intake details, Idaho House rules and Utah's full current consolidation are explicitly unread, and Vermont's September 2027 powers must not be read as operative 2026 law. Every row is marked runtimeIntegrated false: nothing in the game reads any of them yet.
answer.summary: Complete for all 51 jurisdictions. ethics-routing-research.json in the verified package carries 51 rows with zero wholly unresearched jurisdictions, each giving the body that hears a legislative ethics complaint, the proceeding term, the chamber arrangement, the primary authority, routing notes and per-row limits, every row with official sources. Routing must apply the subject's role, the complaint topic, the chamber and the stage rather than substituting one commission per state name. Named distinctions that a single-body model would get wrong: Ohio legislative subjects go to the Joint Legislative Ethics Committee, not the separately named Ohio Ethics Commission; Maryland sends legislative complaints other than financial-disclosure matters to its Joint Committee on Legislative Ethics; Illinois separates Legislative Inspector General intake and investigation from Legislative Ethics Commission hearings; Minnesota and Alaska both have separate chamber-level routes; North Carolina's statutory name is Legislative Ethics Committee, with State Ethics Commission referral authority. South Carolina splits statutory investigation from chamber-rule-only complaints, Florida sends findings to the chamber for sanction, Connecticut splits confidential referee probable-cause from public Board adjudication, Pennsylvania splits confidential proceedings from public final orders, and Rhode Island's express legislative coverage and Oregon's protected-conduct dismissal rule must not be flattened into one immunity rule.

title: Which body hears a legislative ethics complaint, state by state
usableAnswer: A row per state for those twenty-seven, in the same shape as the twenty-four already answered: the body's own name, the term the state uses for the proceeding, whether the two chambers run separate panels or share one, and the citation that establishes it. Where a state routes legislator complaints to a general ethics commission rather than a legislative panel, say so rather than leaving the row blank.
whyItMatters: A press matter about a legislator picks its procedure from a registry that currently holds one entry, Kentucky, so the same story reads identically in fifty states and the one place-specific detail a player would recognize is missing. Twenty-four jurisdictions are already answered with their authorities and are ours to integrate; these twenty-seven are the only ones that still need looking up, and asking for all fifty-one again would spend the answer on rows that are already in hand.
